title: Suhayb the Roman
hookLine: who gave all his wealth to be allowed to emigrate, and was told, the trade was profitable (sirah)

cards: The road out of Mecca is blocked. A man is trying to leave for Medina, where the Prophet and his companions have gone, and some men of Quraysh stand in his way. Their point is about money.
You came here with nothing, they tell him. You got rich among us. And now you want to walk off with all of it?
Not a chance. He could argue. He could fight.
He could turn back and wait for a better day. Instead he asks them a question. Today: Suhayb, called the Roman.

teach.h: IF I GIVE YOU MY WEALTH, WILL YOU LET ME GO?
teach.b: The story is told in the early biographies of the Prophet. Suhayb's question was simple: if I give you my wealth, will you let me go? They said yes.
He told them where it was, handed it over, and left for Medina with nothing.
When word reached the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, he said, as the biographies tell it: Suhayb has profited. Suhayb has profited. Why the Roman?

Tradition says Suhayb was an Arab by birth, carried off as a child, who grew up among the Byzantines, the Romans of that time, until his speech carried their accent, and who later came to Mecca and made his living as a trader.
So he knew exactly what money was, and what a deal was. That's what makes the Prophet's words land. He didn't call Suhayb generous, or brave.

teach.h: A TRADER'S WORD TO A TRADER.
teach.b: He spoke a trader's language back to a trader: you've made a profit.

teach.h: ONE WHO SELLS HIS OWN SELF.
teach.b: Some commentators on the Qur'an connect Suhayb to a verse in surah two about a person who sells his own self, seeking the good pleasure of God.

Not every commentator links the verse to him, and the verse speaks for itself either way. The picture is the same: everything on one side of the scale, and on the other, the road to where he wanted to be.
The trade the Prophet praised was not a loss dressed up as virtue. He called it a profit.

how: Muslims tell Suhayb's story from the early biographies of the Prophet, and some commentators read it alongside surah 2:207, about one who sells himself seeking God's pleasure.

practice: Bring to mind one small comfort that stands between you and something good: an extra hour of scrolling that could be a call to your mother, a lie-in that could be a dawn prayer, if you pray, or a walk.
Hold both sides of the trade for a few breaths, and choose one, small but real.

wordCard.voice: Suhayb. The trader who handed over his wealth to be let go to Medina, and was told by the Prophet that he had profited. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: Suhayb al-Rumi, Suhayb the Roman.

carryVoice: Your line: a profitable trade. Everything given, and still called a gain. See you tomorrow.
